title: Reading Drill — Sorting bricks for reuse — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Sorting bricks for reuse — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Brackenton, work on reusable bricks being mixed with cracked pieces had already produced a small collection of sample checks. The site supervisor used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the proportion of intact bricks recovered.

**B** The group kept sorting before transport for the new trial, which was planned to run for six weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that mortar left on the bricks should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
